diagram_math_checks.objects_and_maps: U=range(P_0), U-perp=ker(P_0), V_X={u+Xu:u in U}; top map J_X:U->V_X is u->u+Xu. The two arrows leaving V_X are pi_U|V_X:V_X->U and pi_U-perp|V_X:V_X->U-perp; left vertical map is I_U and lower map is X:U->U-perp.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Statement and proof steps 1.1, 1.2 and 2.1 give this splitting, graph and bijective projection. Every drawn arrow has the indicated domain and codomain.

diagram_math_checks.relation: pi_U|V_X composed with J_X equals I_U, and J_X composed with pi_U|V_X equals I_V_X.
diagram_math_checks.justification: For u in U, orthogonality gives pi_U(u+Xu)=u. Every vector of V_X has a unique such expression by step 2.1, so the two top arrows are inverse.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The square commutes: (pi_U-perp|V_X) J_X = X I_U = X.
diagram_math_checks.justification: pi_U-perp(u+Xu)=Xu by the orthogonal splitting from step 1.1 and the definition of V_X. Both paths have domain U and codomain U-perp.

diagram_math_checks.relation: In the ordered splitting U direct-sum U-perp, H has blocks (0,B*;B,0), with B:U->U-perp and B*:U-perp->U. H=P′(0) for P(t)=P(tB), with real curve parameter t.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 2.2 differentiates Hermiticity and idempotence to give zero diagonal blocks and adjoint off-diagonal blocks, then realizes every such H by this graph curve. No real coordinate-plane representation or dimensional restriction is imposed.
